title: Rotation and overlap
hints: Picture a p orbital on either carbon.
Twist one set of lobes out of parallel alignment.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: Rotation reduces the parallel p-orbital overlap that supplies the pi bond.
statement:
Why does rotating one end of a C=C double bond have a high energy barrier?

[_]{a}

choices: It changes the total electron count.
It turns carbon nuclei into ions.
It requires breaking every C–H bond.
explanations: Rotation does not change electron count.
The barrier is due to orbital alignment.
The relevant interaction is the C=C pi overlap.
